passages.title: Should Schools Limit Smartphone Use?
passages.text:
Smartphones are part of students’ daily lives. They help students contact their families, check information, and use learning applications. However, having a phone nearby during every lesson can make it harder for some students to concentrate. Schools should therefore limit non-academic phone use during lessons, while still allowing phones when teachers decide they support learning.

One reason for this policy is that notifications can interrupt attention. A student who checks a message may miss an instruction and then need the teacher to repeat it. Phones can also make group discussions less effective when students focus on their screens instead of listening to one another. Clear limits can help students give their attention to the task and participate more actively.

A second reason is that technology is most useful when it has a clear purpose. Teachers may ask students to use a phone to look up a word, complete a short quiz, or photograph information from a classroom activity. If phones are used only when needed, students can benefit from these tools without allowing unrelated apps to take over the lesson.

Some parents worry that students may need to contact their families during the school day. This concern is reasonable, especially in an emergency. A school policy can address it by allowing students to contact family members through the school office or by making exceptions when a teacher gives permission. Limiting unnecessary use does not mean removing every useful or important use.

For these reasons, schools should set clear and fair rules rather than impose a complete ban. Phones can be kept away during ordinary learning activities and used when a teacher gives permission. Such a policy protects lesson time while recognising that smartphones can also be useful tools.

passages.title: Should Homework Be Reduced?
passages.text:
Homework is a common part of school life, but people disagree about how much students should receive. Some teachers and parents believe that homework is important because it gives students another chance to practise what they have learned. When students solve problems or review vocabulary at home, they may remember the material more clearly. Homework can also help students develop responsibility and learn to manage their time.

On the other hand, too much homework can create problems. Students may have several assignments due on the same day, leaving little time for sleep, exercise, hobbies, or family activities. If a task takes many hours, students may rush through it simply to finish. In that situation, the amount of homework does not necessarily lead to better learning.

The value of homework also depends on its quality. A short task that asks students to explain an idea in their own words may be more useful than many repetitive exercises. Teachers can coordinate deadlines so that students are not overloaded. They can also make sure that assignments are connected to lesson goals and that students understand what they are expected to do.

Both sides raise reasonable points. Homework can support learning when it gives students meaningful practice, but excessive or repetitive tasks can become a burden. Schools should not necessarily remove homework. Instead, teachers should consider its purpose, length, and timing. A smaller amount of well-planned homework may help students learn while leaving enough time for other important parts of life.

passages.topic: The Hidden Cost of Fast Fashion
passages.title: The Hidden Cost of Fast Fashion
passages.text:
Fast fashion makes new styles available at low prices and allows shoppers to change their wardrobes frequently. For people with limited budgets, inexpensive clothing can seem like a practical choice. However, the low price shown on a label does not always reflect the wider cost of producing, transporting, and disposing of clothes.

Many fast-fashion items are designed to be worn for a short time. When clothing is made quickly and sold at very low prices, shoppers may feel encouraged to buy more than they need. Clothes that are rarely worn may eventually be thrown away. Producing fabric, dyeing materials, and transporting finished products also require resources and energy. These processes can create waste and pollution if they are not managed responsibly.

It would be unfair to suggest that every shopper can simply buy expensive, ethically produced clothing. Some people have little choice because affordable options are important to their household budgets. The responsibility should not fall on consumers alone. Clothing companies can provide clearer information about how products are made, improve working conditions, and design items that last longer.

Consumers can also take realistic steps. They can repair clothes, exchange items with friends, choose second-hand clothing when suitable, or pause before buying something they may rarely wear. These actions will not solve every problem in the fashion industry, but they can reduce unnecessary consumption.

Fast fashion is not only a question of personal style or price. It also raises questions about resources, waste, and responsibility. Shoppers should not be blamed for every problem, but both companies and consumers can make more thoughtful choices. Longer-lasting clothes and more transparent production are better goals than constantly buying the newest trend.

passages.topic: How Screen Time Relates to Sleep
passages.title: How Screen Time Relates to Sleep
passages.text:
Many teenagers use phones, tablets, or computers in the evening. These devices can help them finish schoolwork and stay in touch with friends. However, using screens late at night may be linked to shorter sleep. Notifications can keep people mentally active, and time spent watching videos or playing games may delay the moment they go to bed.

A small survey at one senior high school asked 120 students about their recreational screen use after 7 p.m. and their usual sleep duration on school nights. Among students who reported more than three hours of recreational screen use after 7 p.m., the average reported sleep duration was 6.4 hours. Among students who reported one hour or less, the average was 7.5 hours.

The figures show a difference between the two groups, but they do not prove that screen use alone caused the difference. Other factors may affect sleep, including homework, travel time, caffeine, family routines, or health. The survey also relied on students’ own reports, so the answers may not be exact. A larger study would be needed to understand the relationship more clearly.

Even with these limits, students can try simple habits that support better rest. They might set a time to stop recreational screen use, silence non-essential notifications, and keep a regular bedtime. These steps do not require students to stop using technology completely. The goal is to make evening routines more balanced and to notice whether changes help them feel more rested.

passages.title: Renewable Energy in Our Communities
passages.text:
TEXT A – Why Communities Should Move Faster
Communities should expand renewable energy projects more quickly. Solar panels and wind turbines can produce electricity without burning fuel while they operate. They can also reduce dependence on a single energy source. In some areas, schools, public buildings, and homes have roofs that could support solar panels, making local projects possible.

Critics point out that sunlight and wind are not available at the same level all the time. This is a real challenge, but it is not a reason to delay every project. Communities can combine different energy sources, improve electricity networks, and use energy storage where it is suitable. Local authorities can begin with projects that match their needs and budgets, then expand as experience grows.

Renewable energy projects may require careful planning and initial investment. Still, waiting for a perfect solution can also delay useful improvements. Communities should set realistic targets and begin with practical projects while continuing to improve the systems that support them.

TEXT B – Why Careful Planning Matters
Renewable energy can contribute to a cleaner energy system, but communities should plan projects carefully rather than expand them without considering local conditions. A solar project may work well in one location but be less suitable in another. Wind projects also depend on local wind conditions, available land, and the needs of nearby residents.

Supporters often argue that storage and improved electricity networks can help manage changes in solar and wind power. These options are important, but they may require investment, technical planning, and time. Communities should compare costs, discuss possible effects with residents, and consider how renewable sources will work alongside other reliable sources of electricity.

Careful planning does not mean rejecting renewable energy. It means choosing projects that are suitable, affordable, and supported by the people who will live with them. A gradual approach can help communities avoid costly mistakes and build public trust.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?
choices: Schools should remove all digital devices from students’ lives.
Students should be allowed to use smartphones whenever they wish.
Schools should limit unrelated phone use during lessons but allow purposeful use.
Parents should contact teachers every time students use a phone.
Learning applications are less useful than printed books.
questions.evidence: Schools should therefore limit non-academic phone use during lessons, while still allowing phones when teachers decide they support learning.
questions.explanation: Jawaban C benar karena penulis mendukung pembatasan penggunaan ponsel yang tidak berhubungan dengan pelajaran, tetapi tetap mengizinkan penggunaan yang membantu belajar. Bukti dari teks: paragraf 1 menyatakan bahwa sekolah perlu membatasi penggunaan non-akademik, sementara paragraf 5 menolak larangan total.

questions.prompt: Which statement best expresses the writer’s main claim?
choices: Every student should own a smartphone.
Schools should create clear limits on non-academic smartphone use during lessons.
Teachers should stop using digital learning applications.
Parents should be responsible for all classroom rules.
Smartphones should be used only outside school.
questions.evidence: Schools should therefore limit non-academic phone use during lessons, while still allowing phones when teachers decide they support learning.
questions.explanation: Jawaban B benar karena itulah pendapat utama yang ingin dibuktikan penulis: penggunaan ponsel yang tidak berkaitan dengan pelajaran perlu dibatasi selama pembelajaran. Bukti dari teks: paragraf 1 menyampaikan usulan tersebut secara langsung.

questions.prompt: Which detail from the passage best supports the idea that phone notifications can disturb learning?
choices: Students use phones to contact their families.
Some teachers use phones for short quizzes.
Parents may worry about emergencies.
A student may miss an instruction after checking a message, causing the teacher to repeat it.
Some schools keep phones away during ordinary activities.
questions.evidence: A student who checks a message may miss an instruction and then need the teacher to repeat it.
questions.explanation: Jawaban D benar karena contoh itu menunjukkan akibat langsung dari gangguan notifikasi: siswa melewatkan instruksi dan guru harus mengulanginya. Bukti dari teks: paragraf 2 menjelaskan bahwa siswa yang memeriksa pesan dapat melewatkan instruksi.

questions.prompt: The word “purposeful” in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ....
choices: done for a clear reason or goal.
completed in a hurry.
difficult to understand.
done without any planning.
not connected to a lesson.
questions.evidence: A second reason is that technology is most useful when it has a clear purpose.
questions.explanation: Jawaban A benar. “Purposeful” berarti dilakukan dengan tujuan yang jelas. Dalam teks, ponsel digunakan untuk kegiatan belajar tertentu. Bukti dari teks: paragraf 3 memberi contoh penggunaan ponsel untuk mencari arti kata, mengerjakan kuis, atau memotret informasi pelajaran.

questions.prompt: What can be inferred about the writer’s view of homework?
choices: All homework should be removed immediately.
Homework is useful only for students who get high marks.
The amount of homework matters more than its purpose.
Homework can be helpful, but its design and amount should be considered carefully.
Students learn best when they spend all their free time studying.
questions.evidence: Homework can support learning when it gives students meaningful practice, but excessive or repetitive tasks can become a burden.
questions.explanation: Jawaban D benar. Penulis mengakui manfaat pekerjaan rumah, tetapi juga menjelaskan masalah jika tugas terlalu banyak atau berulang. Jadi, tugas perlu dirancang dengan baik. Bukti dari teks: paragraf 4 menyatakan bahwa PR dapat membantu jika bermakna, tetapi tugas berlebihan dapat menjadi beban.

questions.prompt: Which words best describe the writer’s tone?
choices: Angry and accusing.
Balanced and reasonable.
Humorous and playful.
Fearful and uncertain.
Sarcastic and dismissive.
questions.evidence: Both sides raise reasonable points.
questions.explanation: Jawaban B benar karena penulis menjelaskan alasan dari kedua sisi sebelum memberikan saran. Penulis tidak menyerang salah satu pihak. Bukti dari teks: paragraf 1 menjelaskan manfaat PR, paragraf 2 menjelaskan kekurangannya, dan paragraf 4 memberi kesimpulan yang mempertimbangkan keduanya.

questions.prompt: Which statement is an opinion rather than a directly verifiable detail from the passage?
choices: Some students have several assignments due on the same day.
Homework can include reviewing vocabulary at home.
Teachers can coordinate assignment deadlines.
Students may have less time for hobbies when they have many assignments.
A smaller amount of well-planned homework is the best approach for schools.
questions.evidence: A smaller amount of well-planned homework may help students learn while leaving enough time for other important parts of life.
questions.explanation: Jawaban E benar karena kalimat itu berisi penilaian atau saran penulis tentang pendekatan terbaik. Pilihan lain menjelaskan keadaan atau kemungkinan yang disebutkan dalam teks. Bukti dari teks: paragraf 4 menyatakan bahwa sekolah sebaiknya mempertimbangkan jumlah, tujuan, dan waktu pemberian PR.

questions.prompt: What is the function of the second paragraph in the passage?
choices: It gives an opposing view by explaining possible disadvantages of too much homework.
It repeats the benefits of homework using different examples.
It introduces a new topic unrelated to homework.
It provides a final solution before presenting the issue.
It explains how students should complete every assignment.
questions.evidence: On the other hand, too much homework can create problems.
questions.explanation: Jawaban A benar karena paragraf kedua memperkenalkan sisi yang berlawanan dengan paragraf pertama, yaitu dampak negatif jika PR terlalu banyak. Bukti dari teks: paragraf 1 membahas manfaat PR, sedangkan paragraf 2 dimulai dengan “On the other hand” dan menjelaskan kekurangannya.

questions.topic: The Hidden Cost of Fast Fashion
questions.prompt: Which concern about the writer’s position is acknowledged in paragraph 3?
choices: All clothing companies already provide complete information about production.
Second-hand clothing is always more expensive than new clothing.
Some people need affordable clothing and cannot always choose more expensive alternatives.
Consumers are never able to influence the fashion industry.
Fast fashion has no connection to waste or pollution.
questions.evidence: Some people have little choice because affordable options are important to their household budgets.
questions.explanation: Jawaban C benar karena penulis mengakui bahwa sebagian orang membutuhkan pakaian dengan harga terjangkau dan tidak selalu mampu membeli pilihan yang lebih mahal. Bukti dari teks: paragraf 3 menyebutkan bahwa pilihan terjangkau penting bagi anggaran rumah tangga sebagian orang.

questions.topic: The Hidden Cost of Fast Fashion
questions.prompt: Which conclusion is best supported by the article?
choices: Consumers should stop buying all new clothing.
Only shoppers are responsible for problems in the fashion industry.
Affordable clothing should no longer be available.
Fast fashion has no negative effects if clothes are inexpensive.
Both clothing companies and consumers can take practical steps towards more responsible fashion.
questions.evidence: Shoppers should not be blamed for every problem, but both companies and consumers can make more thoughtful choices.
questions.explanation: Jawaban E benar karena penulis membahas tanggung jawab perusahaan dan konsumen. Perusahaan dapat memperbaiki produksi, sedangkan konsumen dapat mengurangi pembelian yang tidak perlu. Bukti dari teks: paragraf 3 membahas tanggung jawab perusahaan dan paragraf 4 membahas langkah yang dapat dilakukan konsumen.

questions.topic: The Hidden Cost of Fast Fashion
questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the article?
choices: Fast fashion offers low prices, but its wider effects mean that companies and consumers should make more responsible choices.
Second-hand clothing is the only suitable choice for every shopper.
Fashion trends should be followed more carefully by teenagers.
Clothing companies should stop producing different styles.
The price of clothing is the only factor shoppers should consider.
questions.evidence: Fast fashion is not only a question of personal style or price. It also raises questions about resources, waste, and responsibility.
questions.explanation: Jawaban A benar karena artikel membahas harga murah fast fashion, dampaknya terhadap lingkungan dan sumber daya, serta tanggung jawab perusahaan dan pembeli. Bukti dari teks: paragraf 1–5 membahas harga, dampak produksi dan limbah, serta pilihan yang lebih bertanggung jawab.

questions.topic: The Hidden Cost of Fast Fashion
questions.prompt: Which statement best expresses the writer’s central claim?
choices: Every shopper must buy only second-hand clothing.
More responsible choices by both companies and consumers can help address the wider costs of fast fashion.
Low prices are always a sign of poor-quality clothing.
Clothing production should take place only in local communities.
Personal style is more important than environmental concerns.
questions.evidence: Shoppers should not be blamed for every problem, but both companies and consumers can make more thoughtful choices.
questions.explanation: Jawaban B benar karena penulis menekankan bahwa perusahaan dan konsumen sama-sama dapat mengambil langkah yang lebih bertanggung jawab. Bukti dari teks: paragraf 5 menyatakan bahwa perusahaan dan konsumen dapat membuat pilihan yang lebih bijak.

questions.topic: How Screen Time Relates to Sleep
questions.prompt: Which survey result supports the idea that longer evening screen use is associated with shorter sleep?
choices: All 120 students used screens for exactly three hours.
Students who used screens for more than three hours reported an average of 6.4 hours of sleep, compared with 7.5 hours for the one-hour-or-less group.
The survey proved that screens are the only cause of poor sleep.
Students who used screens for one hour or less never used technology during the day.
The school asked students about their favourite games.
questions.evidence: Among students who reported more than three hours of recreational screen use after 7 p.m., the average reported sleep duration was 6.4 hours. Among students who reported one hour or less, the average was 7.5 hours.
questions.explanation: Jawaban B benar karena pilihan ini membandingkan dua angka yang diberikan dalam survei. Kelompok dengan penggunaan layar lebih lama melaporkan waktu tidur rata-rata yang lebih singkat. Bukti dari teks: paragraf 2 mencatat rata-rata 6,4 jam dan 7,5 jam untuk dua kelompok tersebut.

questions.topic: How Screen Time Relates to Sleep
questions.prompt: The word “associated” in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ....
choices: completely separate from.
always caused by.
difficult to measure.
connected or linked to.
impossible to explain.
questions.evidence: using screens late at night may be linked to shorter sleep.
questions.explanation: Jawaban D benar. “Associated” berarti berhubungan atau berkaitan. Kata ini tidak berarti bahwa satu hal pasti menyebabkan hal lainnya. Bukti dari teks: paragraf 3 menjelaskan bahwa data menunjukkan perbedaan, tetapi tidak membuktikan bahwa penggunaan layar adalah satu-satunya penyebab.

questions.topic: How Screen Time Relates to Sleep
questions.prompt: What is the most reasonable conclusion that can be drawn from the survey?
choices: Reducing evening screen use will certainly add exactly one hour of sleep.
All students who use screens at night have sleep problems.
The results show a relationship worth examining, but they do not prove that screen use causes shorter sleep.
The survey results apply equally to every teenager.
Students should never use phones or computers after school.
questions.evidence: The figures show a difference between the two groups, but they do not prove that screen use alone caused the difference.
questions.explanation: Jawaban C benar karena survei menunjukkan hubungan antara penggunaan layar dan lama tidur, tetapi belum membuktikan sebab-akibat. Teks juga menyebutkan faktor lain yang mungkin berpengaruh. Bukti dari teks: paragraf 3 menyatakan bahwa angka tersebut tidak membuktikan penggunaan layar sebagai satu-satunya penyebab.

questions.topic: How Screen Time Relates to Sleep
questions.prompt: How does the writer present the survey findings?
choices: As final proof that all screen use is harmful.
As a reason to ban digital devices from schools.
As an unimportant result that should be ignored.
As a personal complaint about teenagers.
As useful information that should be interpreted carefully because the survey has limits.
questions.evidence: The survey also relied on students’ own reports, so the answers may not be exact. A larger study would be needed to understand the relationship more clearly.
questions.explanation: Jawaban E benar karena penulis menyampaikan hasil survei, tetapi juga menjelaskan keterbatasannya. Nada penulis informatif dan berhati-hati, bukan menakut-nakuti. Bukti dari teks: paragraf 3 menyebutkan bahwa survei hanya dilakukan di satu sekolah dan berdasarkan laporan siswa sendiri.

questions.prompt: Which statement is an opinion rather than a verifiable detail presented in the two texts?
choices: Text A mentions solar panels and wind turbines as renewable energy technologies.
Text B says that local conditions can affect whether a project is suitable.
Text A suggests that communities can combine different energy sources.
Communities should always expand renewable energy as quickly as possible, even when local planning is incomplete.
Text B mentions that projects may require investment and technical planning.
questions.evidence: Careful planning does not mean rejecting renewable energy. It means choosing projects that are suitable, affordable, and supported by the people who will live with them.
questions.explanation: Jawaban D benar karena kata “should always” menunjukkan penilaian atau pendapat tentang tindakan yang sebaiknya dilakukan. Pilihan lain merujuk pada informasi yang memang disebutkan dalam teks. Bukti dari teks: Text A mendukung perluasan yang lebih cepat, tetapi tetap menyebut perlunya target realistis; Text B menekankan perencanaan yang hati-hati.

questions.prompt: How do Text A and Text B relate to each other?
choices: Text B completely rejects renewable energy and argues for using only fossil fuels.
Text A supports faster development, while Text B adds caution about local conditions, costs, and planning.
Both texts argue that renewable energy projects should be stopped.
Text A discusses health, while Text B discusses school education.
Text B repeats every point in Text A without adding a different perspective.
questions.evidence:
Communities should set realistic targets and begin with practical projects while continuing to improve the systems that support them.

TEXT B – Why Careful Planning Matters
Renewable energy can contribute to a cleaner energy system, but communities should plan projects carefully rather than expand them without considering local conditions.
questions.explanation: Jawaban B benar karena kedua penulis mendukung energi terbarukan, tetapi menekankan hal yang berbeda. Text A mendorong kemajuan lebih cepat, sedangkan Text B menekankan perencanaan. Bukti dari teks: Text A meminta masyarakat mulai dengan proyek praktis; Text B meminta proyek dipilih sesuai kondisi, biaya, dan dukungan warga.

questions.prompt: How does the writer of Text A respond to the concern that solar and wind power are not always available?
choices: The writer says that changes in sunlight and wind do not exist.
The writer argues that communities should stop using electricity.
The writer suggests combining energy sources, improving electricity networks, and using storage where suitable.
The writer claims that every home must install a wind turbine.
The writer says that local conditions are never important.
questions.evidence: Communities can combine different energy sources, improve electricity networks, and use energy storage where it is suitable.
questions.explanation: Jawaban C benar karena penulis mengakui bahwa tenaga surya dan angin tidak selalu tersedia, lalu menawarkan beberapa cara untuk mengatasi tantangan tersebut. Bukti dari teks: paragraf 2 Text A menyebut kombinasi sumber energi, jaringan listrik yang lebih baik, dan penyimpanan energi.

questions.prompt: Which conclusion is best supported by both texts?
choices: Renewable energy projects should be expanded without considering costs or local conditions.
Communities should choose between renewable energy and reliable electricity, because they cannot have both.
Renewable energy is unsuitable for every community.
Only national governments can make decisions about local energy projects.
Communities can benefit from renewable energy when projects are practical, carefully planned, and suited to local needs.
questions.evidence: It means choosing projects that are suitable, affordable, and supported by the people who will live with them.
questions.explanation: Jawaban E benar karena kedua teks mendukung energi terbarukan, tetapi sama-sama mengakui perlunya proyek yang realistis dan sesuai kebutuhan setempat. Bukti dari teks: Text A menyarankan proyek praktis dengan target realistis; Text B menekankan kesesuaian, biaya, dan dukungan masyarakat.
